name: private-views
title: Private views
description: Sends each viewer only what they may see, by a policy of hidden fields and reveal conditions.

facilities.description: Policy-driven per-viewer redaction and client view helpers

infrastructure.deployedReason: Local library; no service is deployed by this package.

text.purpose: `private-views` makes the one thing every shared activity with secrets needs: a function `viewFor(state, viewer, policy)` that returns what one viewer may see. The policy lists hidden fields (`players[].cards`, `deck`, `table.secret`), who may see each one (its owner, listed roles, listed array positions, a flag on the item, or a named condition of the policy) and how it is concealed (set to null, removed or masked; per element for arrays). Viewers are participants, spectators and displays; a display never has an id, so it can never count as an owner. The state is never changed. The same component carries the small client side: the envelope every view has (version, room, who it is for, whether it is a display) and the rule for which arriving view to keep. Records grouped by owner (a game's per-player hidden facts) are redacted by `redact(viewerId, records)`, the form the turn engine uses.
text.userInputs: No installer settings. The policy is supplied by the application or by the component that owns the state (for example the game rules component).
text.integration: Server: define one `Policy` for the state type and call `viewFor(state, viewerOf(role, id), policy)` once per connection when the state changes; send each connection its own result. Use `project` to build the view shape from the state, `decorate` to add what only this viewer gets (legal actions, a prompt), and `youField` and `displayField` to tell the client who it is. Clients: `accept(incoming, current, mode)` (web) or `PrivateViews.isNewer` and `matchesMode` (Apple) and `isNewer` and `matchesMode` (Android) keep the newest view and refuse a player view on a display connection and the reverse. `examples/consumer.ts` shows a card table. The turn-engine uses this component through its `private-views` requirement. `redact(viewerId, records)` (server) is the record form: each `HiddenRecord` has an owner, open facts everyone sees, hidden facts only the owner sees, and a `revealed` map naming hidden keys now public (`true`, or the indexes of an array); a null viewer is a display and sees only revealed facts.
text.verification: Required-local: `node --test tests/web.test.ts` checks owners, spectators and displays, removal, nulling, masking and filtering of hidden fields, reveal by listed positions, flags and conditions, roles, projection, decoration, that the state is unchanged, a scan that no viewer's serialised view contains another participant's secrets, `redact` (owner, other viewer, display, revealed index lists, copies, a no-leak scan over every viewer), the client's newest-view and mode rules and the example. Platform: `python3 tests/native.py apple` compiles and runs the Swift envelope checks against `tests/fixtures/views.json`; `python3 tests/native.py android` compiles the Kotlin checks (needs kotlinc, not installed on the authoring machine, so not run there).
text.scenarios: A card table sends Ann her own cards and face-down placeholders for Bob's, except the card Bob has shown. A spectator and a table display see the same public view, and a display whose connection carries a participant id still sees nothing private. At the end of a round a condition reveals every score to everyone. A late reply to an action arrives after a newer pushed view and is ignored.
text.updates: Patch updates replace files; no persisted-state migration. A policy change is a change to what leaves the server, so applications should re-run their no-leak test (the scan in this component's tests is a model) after changing one.

agentInstructions: Select this component for any application where participants hold information others must not see (hidden hands, private notes, hidden scores) or where a public screen must show less than a player's screen. Write the policy with the owner of the state. Connect `private-views` to the engine that builds per-connection messages.
developerInstructions: Write one policy per state type and keep a no-leak test like the one in `tests/web.test.ts` for it: serialise every viewer's view and search it for the secrets of everyone else. Supply no accounts or keys.

suitability.notes: Pure functions. Cost grows with state size times viewers because each view is a deep copy.
